title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
abstract: arXiv:2610.31558v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: \emph{Continuous-space} attacks find prompts that trigger malicious behaviors, such as overthinking, in black-box LLMs by sampling or optimizing over a low-dimensional Gaussian latent space and decoding it to text through a \emph{random mapping} and nearest-token lookup. Because the random mapping is not learned from language, its prompts can be highly unnatural, and as such easily detectable through input guardrails, and the risk estimates they yield are not grounded in natural prompts. In this paper, we demonstrate that the same continuous latent-space framework can be coupled directly to a learned generative distribution over language, a continuous diffusion language model (dLLM), which removes the artificial random mapping while preserving the standard-Gaussian latent formulation and the downstream sampling or optimization procedure. translated_title: 面向困惑度感知黑盒攻击的扩散语言模型
translated_abstract: 连续空间攻击通过在低维高斯潜空间中进行采样或优化，并将其通过随机映射和最近token查找解码为文本，从而找到能够触发黑盒大语言模型恶意行为（如过度思考）的提示词。由于这种随机映射并非从语言中学习得到，其生成的提示词可能非常不自然，因此容易通过输入防护机制被检测到，且其产生的风险估计也并未建立在自然提示的基础之上。在本文中，我们证明可以将同样的连续潜空间框架直接与从语言中学习得到的生成分布——连续扩散语言模型（dLLM）——相耦合，从而消除人为引入的随机映射，同时保留标准高斯潜空间形式以及下游的采样或优化流程。我们在两种设置下评估了该方法：使用 RareTrap 的基于采样的估计以及…
tldr: 该论文提出将连续潜空间攻击框架与连续扩散语言模型（dLLM）直接耦合，以学习到的语言生成分布取代人工随机映射，从而生成更自然、更难被防护机制检测且基于自然提示的黑盒攻击提示词。
en_tdlr: This paper couples the continuous latent-space attack framework directly to a continuous diffusion language model (dLLM), replacing the artificial random mapping with a learned generative distribution over language to produce more natural, less detectable black-box attack prompts grounded in natural language.
